children: By Bharath Rajeswaran

Indian shares traded little changed on Thursday, as an intensifying Middle East conflict kept crude prices above the $100 per barrel mark, while investors awaited key U.S. data before the Federal Reserve's policy next week.
The Nifty 50
edged down 0.01% to 23,429.25 and the BSE Sensex
shed 0.01% to 74,759.54 as of 9:36 a.m. IST.
Nine of the 16 major sectors advanced, but the gains were marginal. The broader small-caps
and mid-caps
were flat.
The Nifty and Sensex settled at three-month lows in the previous session as Brent crude oil
surpassed $100. They have fallen in seven out of the last eight sessions, giving up about 3.1% each in that period.
Iran said it attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers in the largest attacks on shipping in the six-month-old conflict.

Higher oil prices are detrimental for India, the world's third-largest importer of the commodity, as they increase the import bill, worsen inflationary pressures and weigh on economic growth and corporate profitability.

"The undertone of markets remains fragile as Brent crossed (the) $100 per barrel mark amid escalating U.S.-Iran tensions, intensifying concerns over inflation and growth," said Rajesh Palviya, head of research at Axis Direct.
Higher oil prices have also left investors nervous ahead of U.S. inflation data, which is likely to influence the Federal Reserve's rate decision next week, said two traders.
ONGC
and Oil India
gained 2% and 2.4%, respectively, aided by higher crude prices that boost revenues and profit margins of upstream oil producers.
Enviro Infra
added 4.4% after receiving a letter of intent (LoI) from Tata Power Renewable Energy for the development of a 180 MW NTPC wind power project in Maharashtra state.
Shakti Pumps
climbed 10.4% after securing a 2.36 billion rupees order from Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company for the supply of 10,000 solar pumps.
